title: Purpose
text:
The open data action toolkit provides guidance on how to measure organizational actions and public engagement with open data. The actions and measures shared in the toolkit were identified from a review of existing research on open data use and measures, supplemented with observations from case studies of 3 local governments in the United States.
The examples provided in the toolkit are based on the data, products, reporting, and press coverage of the organizations who participated in the case study research of the City of Austin, the City of Baton Rouge and Parish of East Baton Rouge, and the City and County of San Francisco.

Organizational Actions
The toolkit first provides examples of actions taken by organizations to support open data use, such as by creatting new data products (datasets, maps, applications, dashboards, narrative, visualizations, initiative websites), educational content, support channels, and opportunities for community interactions.
Learn more about organizational actions.


Data Portal Measures
The toolkit then demonstrates how to measure direct use of data and other assets published on data portals. Measures include views of datasets, maps, dashboards, visualizations, and data stories. Downloads of data and requests to API (application programming interface) endpoints for datasets are other measures that are available from data portals. Additional context from asset metadata provides another layer of analysis available to evaluate the completeness and usefulness of overall data catalogs.
Learn how to access web analytics from data portals.


Public Engagement Measures
The toolkit also highlight signals of public engagement that include articles from local news organizations and blogs, events featuring open data, questions for data owners, support requests, public information requests, engagement with support videos and content, and resolutions and directives for publishing new data in response to public demand or government transparency on emerging community issues.
Learn more about monitoring public engagement with open data.


Reporting
Finally, the toolkit shows how regular reporting enables organizations to link government and community priorities with actions and measures of progress.
View examples of reporting, including annual reports, performance dashboards, and blog posts.

Articles
The potential for journalists and researchers to act as intermediaries of open data by synthesizing open data into useful information (Shaharudin et al. 2023) and creating feedback loops to government (Wilson and Chakraborty 2019).

Measures
Article measures include publication, date, topic, department data owners, links to data, and contributions made by the publication staff of new data, visualizations, and tools created in support of the article. The presence of articles demonstrates accessibility of department data for local reporting and public interest.

title: Web Analytics
text:
Web Analytics
Data portals publish the number of page views for data assets on overview pages and through APIs (application programming interface). Tyler Technologies and Esri provide documentation on their use (Tyler Technologies 2022), (Esri, n.d.).

Overview Pages
Dataset overview pages provide important details about the data and lifetime page views and downloads. An example of an overview page is the Issued Construction Permits on the Austin data portal.



Issued Building Permits


In the “About” section, the lifetime views and downloads are shown, which for this dataset consist of 5.38 million views and 82.3 thousand downloads.


APIs (Application programming interfaces)
The Tyler Technologies Discovery API (Socrata Discovery API, n.d.) provides analytic details for all data assets on a data portal that includes lifetime views and downloads, as well as views in the last week and month, providing insights on current public interest. Authentication is not required to access information about published data assets on domain. Tools like Excel and Power BI can easily connect to the API endpoint to make information available for analysis.
Example API endpoint with parameters to retrieve all published data assets by data portal domain:

Austin, Texas

Discovery catalog endpoint: http://api.us.socrata.com/api/catalog/v1?search_context=data.austintexas.gov&published=true&limit=5000

Baton Rouge, Louisiana

Discovery catalog endpoint: http://api.us.socrata.com/api/catalog/v1?search_context=data.brla.gov&published=true&limit=5000

San Francisco, California

Discovery catalog endpoint: http://api.us.socrata.com/api/catalog/v1?search_context=data.sfgov.org&published=true&limit=5000


The following screenshot of a Power BI report demonstrates the type of useful information that can be found about the use of data assets from open data portals. The report and an excel file are available on the code repository for demonstration purposes.



Power BI Report of Discovery API Results




Data Portal Detailed Reports
Data portal publishers have additional analytic data available to them, including measures with date and time information and often share that information publicly.

title: About
text:
The toolkit identifies the types of measures that signal public use and engagement with open data and provides recommendations for regular reporting of actions and resulting activity.
The development of the open data actions and measures toolkit fulfills one part of a dissertation portfolio that focuses on measuring open data use and engagement to serve and empower the public. A review of open data research, public administration theory, and case studies of 3 local governments in the U.S. inform the recommendations.

title: Articles
text:
Data Methods
The City of San Francisco tracks citations to open data and includes notes about the articles and tools in a spreadsheet. Citation tools, like Zotero, may also be used to organize articles.
The following screenshot of a Power BI report demonstrates the number of articles and blog posts related to open data, data reporting, and events initiating open government transparency between 2009 and 2025. Including notes with links to data sources and newspaper can be used to link articles to data products and provide insights to department data publishers on the use of their data.

title: Articles
text:
Equitable Access to News
While new opportunities for rich storytelling through narratives and digital tools created by data reporters, there is also a concern that they are not accessible to everyone (Felle 2016) and depend on access to devices, internet, and subscriptions to news services.

title: Reporting
text: Reporting provides programs the opportunity to link actions to outcomes.

title: Reporting
text:
Annual Reporting
Open data policies can be a driver for reporting by including them as a requirement. For example the open data policy(Baton Rouge and Parish of East Baton Rouge, n.d.) for the City of Baton Rouge and Parish of East Baton Rouge requires on annual reporting that “includes an assessment of progress toward achievement of the goals of the City-Parish’s Open Data BR program (under which all City-Parish open data related activities occur), an assessment of how the City-Parish’s work has furthered or will further the City-Parish’s programmatic priorities, and a description and publication timeline for datasets envisioned to be published by the City-Parish in the following year”. Since 2018, they have published annual reports, including some reports published directly on one of their open data platforms.

The cumulative (lifetime) views, downloads, shares, embeds, and programmatic requests to datasets are provided by default by platforms on individual metadata pages and asset inventories. Programs may also track analytics on a daily basis to show use over time.
